issue_context.title: Find index of item in list
issue_context.body:
### Problem description

I wish I could find the indexes of the first occurrences of specific items in a list (i.e. a column of type list). For a single element this would be similar to doing the following in Python:
```python
l = ["a","b","c","b"]
l.index("b")
# returns 1, the first index of "b"
```

In Polars I would like to be able to do something like this
```python
import polars as pl
df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "id": [1,2,3,4],
        "list": [["A", "B"], ["B", "A"], ["C", "B", "A"], ["D", "A", "C", "B"]]
    }
)
df.filter(pl.col("list").arr.index("A") < pl.col("list").arr.index("B"))
```

which returns
```
shape: (2, 2)
┌─────┬─────────────────────┐
│ id  ┆ list                │
│ --- ┆ ---                 │
│ i64 ┆ list[str]           │
╞═════╪═════════════════════╡
│ 1   ┆ ["A", "B"]          │
├╌╌╌╌╌┼╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌┤
│ 4   ┆ ["D", "A", ... "B"] │
└─────┴─────────────────────┘
```

The use case here is to find all rows where "A" occurs before "B" in the list.
comments:
You can sort of do it with `.arr.eval()`

```
>>> df.filter(
...    pl.col("list").arr.eval(
...       (pl.element() == "A").cast(int)).arr.arg_max()
...    <
...    pl.col("list").arr.eval(
...       (pl.element() == "B").cast(int)).arr.arg_max()
... )
```
```
shape: (2, 2)
┌─────┬─────────────────────┐
│ id  ┆ list                │
│ --- ┆ ---                 │
│ i64 ┆ list[str]           │
╞═════╪═════════════════════╡
│ 1   ┆ ["A", "B"]          │
├╌╌╌╌╌┼╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌┤
│ 4   ┆ ["D", "A", ... "B"] │
└─────┴─────────────────────┘
```

The `.cast(int)` shouldn't be needed - it looks like `.arr.arg_min/max()` return null for non-numeric types. (bug?)

You can do this using `arr.eval()`, but `arg_max()` has to look at every item in the list so it's not going to be quite as performant as a `.index` function would. Maybe there's a faster way to do this. My solution is to first build a function that uses expressions to determine the location of an item within a list:

```python
import polars as pl
from polars import col, when

df = pl.DataFrame({
    "id": [1,2,3,4],
    # I changed your 3rd element to not include A at all so we can hit that edge case
    "list": [['A', 'B'], ['B', 'A'], ['C', 'B', 'D'], ['D', 'A', 'C', 'B']]
})

def loc_of(value):
    # only execute if the item is contained in the list
    return when(col("list").arr.contains(value)).then(
        col("list").arr.eval(
            # create array of True/False, then cast to 1's and 0's
            # arg_max() then finds the first occurrence of 1, i.e. the first occurence of value
            (pl.element() == value).cast(pl.UInt8).arg_max()
        ).arr.first()
    ).otherwise(None) # return null if not found

df.filter(loc_of('A') < loc_of('B'))
```
```
shape: (2, 2)
┌─────┬─────────────────────┐
│ id  ┆ list                │
│ --- ┆ ---                 │
│ i64 ┆ list[str]           │
╞═════╪═════════════════════╡
│ 1   ┆ ["A", "B"]          │
├╌╌╌╌╌┼╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌┤
│ 4   ┆ ["D", "A", ... "B"] │
└─────┴─────────────────────┘
```

@ritchie46 I agree that an `arr.index` function would be a nice enhancement to the list API.

@mcrumiller and @cmdlineluser Thanks a lot for your solutions.  I completely forgot to state that I already got a solution a while back on [stackoverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/72689281/index-operation-on-list-column-data-in-polars). Still, using `arg_max` seems like a much easier solution. I'll still have to compare them for performance.

Nonetheless, none of these solutions will beat a native `arr.index` function and I think it would just make it easier for people to have that directly accessible.
I didn't add the `parallel=True` argument for `arr.eval` but with larger/more lists you'll definitely get a speedup from that.
From discussion: accepted, and should be named `index_of` (details to be iron out about finding the reverse), and should first be implemented as a Series method before a list one
Going to try to work on this next.

I have an extremely minimal proof of concept here of just `Series.index_of`, here: https://github.com/itamarst/polars/tree/5503-series-index_of

Things to do in the design:

* [x] Figure out nulls
* [x] Figure out casting (finding i64 in i8 Series, say)
* [ ] Figure out datetimes and suchlike... probably make sure the types match, then just convert both to physical dtypes?
* [x] Figure out lists
* [x] Figure out arrays
* [ ] Figure out structs (or punt?)
* [ ] Searching for null in Series of dtype null (result is `Some(0)` if series is length 1 or more, otherwise `None`)

At Ritchie's request, switched to actually doing an implementation based on expressions, so that is actually implemented in my current prototype.

Searching _for_ list/array/struct support will likely be out of scope for this pass, and searching _within_ a list will also be out of scope. If I can get the first PR merged I will probably then move on to implement searching within a list, i.e. `pl.col("blah").list.index_of(my_value)`.
I guess this might still be missing the list/array specific functionality the original requester had?
Which I will be doing as follow-up PR.
